decisions: The cross-participant authority audit (map section I14) moves into ally_packet_shape.py, five defs past the roster's eleven. It is upstream of the packet, not downstream: _packet calls _check_cross_participant_authority, _check_declared_classes and _check_aura_arming on every packet it builds, and repriced_for_recipient calls producer_item, so leaving I14 in the residue is a back-edge from two modules. Auditing a packet against its declared authority is part of what a packet is, so the module docstring covers it. ally_packet_shape.py lands at 317 body lines and 8 internal imports, clear of both arms.

The five branch modules the roster names needed the hand carve first: extract_modules.py moves top-level units, and the branches were statements inside derive_item_support_effects. The carve landed one `_<producer>_packets` def per branch and four dispatch tables keyed by AllyProducer, so the defs were nameable. Ledger insertion order is the float-sum trap, so the tables hold the blocks in branch order and both goldens are identical across the carve and the split.

item_support_triggered.py, not the roster's item_support_enchanter: Imperial Mandate's amp and Black Cleaver's siblings are debuffs on enemies, and Cryptbloom heals on a takedown. What the ten blocks share is that an authored event arms them, which is the one idea the module holds.

SupportCtx, the two moment records and _context went to support_context.py rather than into ally_packet_shape.py. support_context.py has six readers, so its own fan-out arm is live and it stays a leaf at six internal imports; ally_packet_shape.py is the vocabulary one packet is built from, and a fight-wide input record is the other half of that sentence, not the same one.

_support_quest_packets travels with _quest_packets, and the cleanse trio with _self_cleanse_packets: each pair is one block and its own helper, and splitting them would make the helper a second module's export with one reader.

schedule_knights_vow stays in the residue. It is not a packet block (it mutates an already-built timeline) but it is the module's other published entry point, and participant_timeline is the one reader of both: moving it would give the tree a second reader module for no gain.

Fallout the tool cannot pay, all of it the coverage-evidence layer binding a packet literal to the module a claim names. Each capability's trigger_stream impl now names the block that builds its packet, so _walk_item's impl loses its default and _SUPPORT_IMPL is gone; item_coverage's 34 support-packet evidence rows are derived from the same capability table; scripts/packet_declarations.py walks the block modules the dispatch tables name rather than one file, which is why PRODUCER_TABLES is published; tests/test_coverage_claims.py reads its packet-site scans off the same registry and mutates the module Command's block lives in; tests/conftest.py monkeypatches the Fimbulwinter mana gate on item_support_everlasting; tests/test_architecture.py enters the five blocks and support_context on FRONT_DOOR_FRONTIER as split leaves; and scripts/literal_defaults_baseline.txt takes support_context.py as a covered root (it is clean) and moves its uncovered-tail ceiling from 89 to 93, which is one uncovered module becoming six with no site added or hidden.
